description: Motion-graphics templates rendered with drawbox/drawtext expressions — no After Effects, no image assets, brand colours from brand.json.

alpha_codec.description: the alpha line: prores4444 (default; ProRes 4444, 16-bit alpha), qtrle (QuickTime Animation, .mov), png (PNG frames, .mov/.mkv), vp9 (VP9 with alpha, .webm/.mkv)

alpha_mode.description: how the colour is written beside the alpha: straight (default, as composited) or premultiplied by the alpha; reported as alpha_mode

argv.description: raw CLI arguments (non-canonical compatibility path; when present every other key is ignored)

audio_stream.description: which audio stream of the input to keep, 0-based in file order (probe.py lists them under audio_streams) -- matters on a multi-track input (dubbed languages, M&E stems); default 0, the first track, same as leaving it unset always did

brand.description: brand.json for colours, font, safe margin

codec.description: video encoder for the re-encode: h264 (x264, the default for SDR), hevc (x265, the default for HDR), av1 (SVT-AV1 or libaom), prores (422 HQ, needs a .mov/.mkv output); HDR sources keep their colour on hevc/av1/prores

drop_alpha.description: the source has alpha and an opaque output is wanted: the alpha is dropped on purpose and a note says so. Without it (or --keep-alpha) an output that loses a used alpha fails the `alpha` step

dry_run.description: print the ffmpeg commands that would run, run nothing

duration.description: hook: seconds the opening card stays up (default 3)

emoji.description: how emoji in the template text are drawn (see caption.py --emoji)

emoji_assets.description: directory of emoji PNGs named by code point (1f389.png); nothing is ever downloaded

emoji_max.description: most emoji overlays one run may build (default 60)

emoji_scale.description: emoji box as a multiple of the line's font size (default 1.0)

fast.description: preview quality: x264 preset veryfast (overrides --preset) for quick iterations

font.description: font family (fontconfig name; default DejaVu Sans, or the --brand file's font)

font_file.description: explicit .ttf/.otf/.ttc path (use this for CJK fonts)

hw.description: encode on the GPU with Apple VideoToolbox (h264/hevc/prores; Apple Silicon only): several times faster, larger files at the same quality; falls back to the CPU encoder, reported, where it cannot apply

json_brief.description: like --json but trimmed: status, output, dry_run, verified, a compact summary of the output probe, this tool's own keys, and the command count instead of the command lines (failures print the full failure document, unchanged)

keep_alpha.description: keep the source's alpha: write the output in an alpha line (--alpha-codec, default prores4444; needs a .mov/.mkv, or .webm for vp9) with the source's colour tags kept, and check the alpha after (the `alpha` verification step). Refused on a source without an alpha plane

lang.description: language code of the text (e.g. ja, zh, ko): the hint that says whether Han-only text is Chinese, Japanese or Korean when a font is picked by script

margin.description: distance from the frame edge in px (default: brand safe_margin, or the --platform safe zone)

no_hw.description: encode on the CPU (x264/x265/SVT-AV1/prores_ks) even when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW=1

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output (refused without it)

plan.description: write the dry run as a plan (inputs fingerprinted, commands, expected output, verify steps) that render.py FILE executes later; implies --dry-run

platform.description: keep the graphic out of this destination's UI: margins become the platform's safe zone (TikTok's description bar and like column, the Reels/Shorts chrome). An explicit --margin wins

position.description: corner for chapter/bug/sticker (default bottom-left / top-right / top-right)

quality.description: encoder quality on the CRF scale (default 18; lower = better; 18 visually lossless for x264/x265, up to 63 for av1); ignored by prores

template.description: graphic to draw: lower-third, title, chapter, progress, countdown, bug, sticker, hook, meme

text_render.description: which renderer draws the template's text: 'auto' (default) uses libass for scripts drawtext cannot shape (Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, Thai, Lao ...) and for emoji overlays, and for multi-line text on FFmpeg 8.0, 8.0.1 and 8.1.0 (their drawtext draws a box at each line break), and drawtext for everything else -- Latin/CJK/Arabic frames are pixel-identical to 1.14 (the drawtext command itself changed: the label is passed as textfile=, not text=); 'ass' always uses libass; 'drawtext' forces the old renderer and is refused for a script it cannot shape

timeout.description: kill an ffmpeg run past this many seconds, kind=timeout (default 1800; 0 = no limit)

title.description: title / chapter / bug / hook text, or lower-third second line

wrap.description: how a label too wide for the frame is broken into lines: 'phrase' (default, 1.16) never breaks inside a word or a hyphen's wrong side, never leaves a lone digit, kana or punctuation on its own line, prefers Japanese sentence ends and particles, and never ends a line on an article or preposition; 'measured' is 1.15's width-only wrap. A label that already fits one line is untouched either way

write_ass.description: where to save the generated ASS when the libass route is used (default: <output stem>_gfx.ass)

name: graphics
